module_title: Early Medieval Period - Dynasties, Temple Architecture, and Travellers
introduction: This level focuses on the major Rajput dynasties and their capitals, the magnificent temple architecture developed during this period, and the vital historical literature produced by scholars like Al-Biruni and Kalhana.

core_concepts.title: Major Rajput Dynasties and Capitals
core_concepts.description: Chandelas (Khajuraho/Mahoba), Paramaras (Dhar, Malwa), Solankis/Chalukyas (Anhilwara, Gujarat), Tomaras (Dhillika or Delhi), and Senas (Bengal). Note: Delhi was originally founded by the Tomara Rajputs (Anangpal).

core_concepts.title: Golden Age of Temple Architecture
core_concepts.description: The Chandelas built the famous 'Khajuraho Temples' (e.g., Kandariya Mahadeva). Vimal Shah, a minister of Solanki ruler Bhima I, built the 'Dilwara Jain Temples' at Mount Abu, and Bhima I built the 'Sun Temple at Modhera'.

core_concepts.title: Literary Development: Rajatarangini
core_concepts.description: Written by Kalhana in the 12th century, 'Rajatarangini' is considered the first authentic historical text of ancient India. It details the history of Kashmir.

core_concepts.title: Al-Biruni and 'Kitab-ul-Hind'
core_concepts.description: Al-Biruni accompanied Mahmud Ghazni to India. He wrote 'Tahqiq-i-Hind' (or Kitab-ul-Hind) in Arabic, providing a precise and critical account of contemporary Indian society, science, religion, and the caste system.

core_concepts.title: Palas and Senas of Bengal
core_concepts.description: The Pala ruler Dharmapala founded the 'Vikramshila University'. Palas were great patrons of Buddhism. They were succeeded by the Senas, who were orthodox Hindus (Jayadeva, author of 'Gita Govinda', lived in the court of Lakshmana Sena).

important_entities.name: Raja Bhoja
important_entities.significance: Ruled from Dhar (MP). Besides being a great warrior, he was a polymath and scholar of Ayurveda, grammar, and architecture. He founded the city of Bhopal (Bhojpal).

important_entities.name: Al-Biruni
important_entities.significance: He became the first Muslim scholar to learn Sanskrit and deeply study the Puranas and Hindu philosophy.

important_entities.name: Chandbardai
important_entities.significance: A friend and court poet of Prithviraj Chauhan who composed the epic poem 'Prithviraj Raso'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often mistakenly attribute the Khajuraho temples to the Guptas or Chauhans. They were exclusively built by the 'Chandela' Rajput dynasty.
Delhi (Dhillika) was not founded by the Chauhans, but by the 'Tomara' Rajput ruler Anangpal in the 8th century. The Chauhans later captured it from the Tomaras.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A quick association to remember famous authors and their prominent works.

exam_strategy_tips: 'Match the following' questions regarding Temples and their builder dynasties are very common (e.g., Modhera Sun Temple - Solankis, Kandariya Mahadeva - Chandelas).
Clearly remember the founders of Buddhist institutions associated with the Pala dynasty (like Odantapuri and Vikramshila).
